owner_words: This needs the kicker part of the setup and have a big green candle to follow from the visual. / Decently big. It is supposed to be like a red candle prior and then a decent size gap up the next day that follows through pretty nicely so MSFT example would work if the next candle from the image was a good green one on a gap up
action: Kicker = a red prior candle, then a decent-size gap up the next day that follows through with a strong green candle closing near its high. Detector positives judged by this rule: keep NVDA 2022-07-19 (si for pos_3; prior red, gap +2.4%, day +5.5%), AMZN 2022-07-19 (pos_4; gap +1.7%, day +3.9%), META 2022-07-15 (pos_5; gap +1.6%, day +4.2%); cut AAPL 2022-07-12 si_3a28b8115c7e (gap 0.6%, day +0.7%, closed low in range), MSFT 2022-07-18 si_32b4fe9bc468 (prior green, closed red), GOOGL 2022-07-18 si_5613f589e2cb (closed red). Note for the detector owner: the detector fires without a green close (K4 is a label only) and without a red prior day, and would not fire on MSFT 2022-07-19 (red prior, gap +1.3%, green close at the high, day +2.1%) because its high stayed under the prior high.

owner_words: Scanner one but also let us have definitions and details for the others. The close above version would be a super oops reversal if it fully engulfs previous day after any version of the oops. Otherwise it is just a scanner oops or Williams oops. / Super Oops engulf = Closes above prior high
action: Oops Reversal = the scanner definition (open < prior close, low < prior low, close > prior close); all 6 detector positives stay Yes. Teach three named versions with definitions and details: (1) Scanner Oops = the main definition above; (2) Williams Oops = opens below the prior LOW and rallies back above it (AAPL 2022-07-13 si_38dec06c4c4a is a Williams Oops but not a Scanner Oops; AAPL 2022-08-09, NVDA 2022-07-05, META 2022-07-13 are both); (3) Super Oops Reversal = any Oops version that fully engulfs the previous day = trades under the prior low AND closes above the prior HIGH (MSFT 2022-07-14 si_944aefc0e9c0, GOOGL 2022-07-05 si_74458acd0081). Item si_38dec06c4c4a (key No for the Scanner Oops) needs its question named Scanner Oops so Williams-Yes is not a defensible second answer. Build: variant questions + lessons; reword the setupCatalog.js essence (owner OK required).

owner_words: Yeah so a slingshot is supposed to be used for an earnings gapper, strong stock, or consolidation after a nice uptrend / And no an earnings gap does not count btw (MSFT and GOOGL 2022-07-27 sent to him as images to look at)
action: Slingshot needs strength behind it: after an earnings gapper, on a strong stock, or a consolidation after a nice uptrend; then the pullback and the recapture of the 4-EMA of the highs. The earnings gap-up day itself does NOT count as the Slingshot trigger. Detector positives: keep AMZN 2022-08-10 (reported 2022-07-28, gapped +10.3% on 07-29, above a rising 50-day). Cut: NVDA 2022-07-27 si_889105c38ed5, META 2022-08-10 si_3384b42db5a6, AAPL 2022-11-30 si_3676408aff39 (downtrend bounces, falling 50-day, no earnings gap behind); MSFT 2022-07-27 si_f8e741ccfb7c and GOOGL 2022-07-27 si_07b6bd12c0d3 (the trigger is the earnings gap day itself, after the 07-26 reports, in downtrends). Report dates verified on the pod from FMP stable/earnings 2026-10-24. Owner was still looking at the MSFT/GOOGL images when this was recorded; reopen if he overrides. Note for the detector owner: S5 (close > SMA50) lets downtrend bounces and earnings gap days through.

owner_words: Yeah these are not slingshots.. it should be after a good rally to the upside and consolidation or after an earnings gapper and consolidation
action: Refines the Slingshot ruling above: the order is (a) a good rally up OR an earnings gapper, THEN (b) a consolidation/pullback, THEN (c) the recapture of the 4-EMA of the highs. MSFT and GOOGL 2022-07-27 confirmed NOT Slingshots (owner looked at the images). AMZN 2022-08-10 stays provisionally (gap 07-29, then 7 sessions of consolidation, recapture 08-10) but is re-examined with fresh examples.

owner_words: You keep using the same charts as examples for like a variety of different setups. I have seen this MSFT example for multiple different ones.
action: Setup examples must be drawn from a wide variety of tickers and dates. The detector fixtures (tests/fixtures/uct_*/pos_*.json) all use the same six mega-caps (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, META, GOOGL) over 2022, so one MSFT chart carries several setup answers. Before any spot/family setup item goes back to the owner: run each detector over the full cap universe and a multi-year window (the way find_candle_examples.py does for candles), keep examples that pass the owner definition, and never reuse a (ticker, asof) across setups. The fixture-based examples are for tests, not teaching.
